statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-15558 is an uncontrolled search path element in the Docker CLI plugin manager (github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager) that leads to local privilege escalation on Windows. Harbor core is built only for Linux. Its binary does not include the cli-plugins/manager package; harbor-core uses github.com/docker/cli only for configuration file handling (cli/config). The vulnerable plugin-discovery code is therefore not present in the harbor-core binary.

Harbor core is built only for Linux. Its binary does not include the cli-plugins/manager package; harbor-core uses github.com/docker/cli only for configuration file handling (cli/config). The vulnerable plugin-discovery code is therefore not present in the harbor-core binary.

This CVE is a plugin search path problem in the Docker CLI plugin manager on Windows (the cli-plugins/manager package). This image runs on Linux and links only the Docker CLI configuration and credentials packages (cli/config), not the plugin manager, so none of the affected code is present.

GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p (CVE-2025-15558) affects github.com/docker/cli from 19.03.0 up to but not including 29.2.0, and only the Windows plugin search path under C:\ProgramData\Docker\cli-plugins. The docker CLI in this image is 29.9.2 and the docker-scout CLI plugin embeds docker/cli 29.6.2, both at or above the fixed version 29.2.0. This image is Linux-only, so the Windows-specific search path does not apply. Scanner data that reports these versions as affected does not match the advisory's fixed version.

The affected code is reached only through the Go binary in the devfile gem, which parses workspace definitions; backup-utility does not invoke it. The fix, docker/cli 29.2.0, cannot be taken here because oras-go v1.2.5 does not compile against the newer docker registry.AuthConfig type. Resolves when oras-go releases a version compatible with the newer docker API.

CVE-2025-15558 is in the Docker CLI plugin manager (github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager). The console vendors github.com/docker/cli only for cli/config (registry authentication, pulled transitively via go-containerregistry); the cli-plugins tree is not vendored or imported, so the vulnerable code is not present in the bridge binary.

CVE-2025-15558 lives in the Docker CLI plugin-manager package (github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager), where the Windows CLI resolves plugin binaries from a directory a low-privileged local attacker can create. The flaw is Windows-only (manager_windows.go, excluded by Go build constraints) while this image is built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, and no upstream fix exists for any docker/cli version. The dhi/tkn image installs the tekton-cli package, which ships only the tkn client binary at /usr/bin/tkn. It contains no Docker daemon and no Docker CLI plugin loader. The only github.com/docker/cli code linked into the binary is the credential-configuration subtree (cli/config with its configfile, credentials, memorystore and types packages), reached through go-containerregistry's authn keychain when `tkn bundle` resolves registry credentials. `go tool nm` on the shipped binary reports zero symbols from cli-plugins, so the vulnerable code is not present in the image. The scanner matches the resolved module version against the advisory range regardless of reachability, so this statement is required to clear the false positive.
